newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian UES says has written own reform plan.
newsitem.headline: Russian UES says has written own reform plan.

text.p: Russian reformers and energy complex officials back a plan to reform national electric company UES that the company itself drew up, UES's economy department chief said on Wednesday.
"In the end they approved practically the whole programme," Sergei Obratsov said in an interview. "(First Deputy Prime Minister) Nemtsov also supported it," he said.
The government is considering how to reform Russia's largest company by sales and staff, in which it has an approximately 52 percent stake, and Nemtsov is in charge of the project.
Nemtsov led a meeting on the issue on Tuesday that was attended by top government and energy complex officials as well as UES investors.
Critics have said UES should be radically restructured and possibly broken up, but top government officials have said government control could be increased over UES and it would not be broken up.

Obratsov said the utility had programmes for 1997-1998 and through 2000. "There is no question of breaking it up," he said, specifically adding that cutting the company into regions to stimulate competition was out of the question.
He said reform would have to be slow, on the basis of a legal framework that still needed to be put in place and would clarify which company activities, such as transport, were monopolistic.

He said UES backed greater competition on the national wholesale market, which buys electricity from regions with energy surpluses and sells to those with shortfalls, to provide for competition on that market.
But he said entry by end-users on the market should be looked at on a company-by-company basis.
"It depends on the economic effectiveness of each company. We need to see for whom it is profitable and for whom it is not."
